name: Hiram College
academic_ranking: Private liberal arts college founded in 1850, accredited by the Higher Learning Commission. Ranked 10th among Midwestern regional liberal arts colleges in the 2026 U.S. News & World Report rankings. Featured in Loren Pope's 'Colleges That Change Lives.' Enrollment approx. 1,026 undergraduates (fall 2024), roughly 30 majors and 38 minors under the 'Hiram Connect' curriculum.
financial_aid: As an NCAA Division III institution, Hiram College does not offer athletic scholarships. Financial aid is available in the form of academic/merit scholarships, need-based grants, and federal/state aid. Exact tuition and aid figures not confirmed from a live authoritative source during research (checked 2026-07).
facilities_notes: Hiram Terriers athletics facilities listed on the athletics site include Fishel Field at Proverbs Park, Charles A. Henry Field at Malmisur Stadium, and Myrtis E. Herndon Field. A specific named softball venue was not clearly confirmed from the softball program page (checked 2026-07).
program_reputation: NCAA Division III women's softball program competing in the Presidents' Athletic Conference (PAC), which Hiram joined July 1, 2024. Team X/Twitter account is @Hiram_SB.
notes: Coaching staff and roster data captured live from hiramterriers.com on 2026-07. Softball coaches directory lists a two-person staff (head coach and one assistant). Roster page listed 18 players for the 2026 season. Tuition figure could not be verified from a live authoritative source and is left null rather than guessed.
